purpose: Recover prior JANUS ocean/UAP/acoustic observations, separate open-source verified acoustic facts from legacy overclaims, and convert the surviving material into controls for the Janus-Echo-Cousteau underwater acoustic search.

legacy_cases_recovered.use_in_cousteau: historical transmedium context only; not an acoustic positive control

legacy_cases_recovered.legacy_claim: periscope plus sonar UAP encounter under Arctic ice
legacy_cases_recovered.corrective_note: Open FOIA-linked command-history research confirms Trepang was conducting weapons-system tests in the Arctic. Publicly circulated photographs lack a demonstrated raw sonar-contact chain; naval target/test explanations are plausible.

legacy_cases_recovered.legacy_claim: declassified SOSUS telemetry, 150+ knot underwater mover, >8000 m depth, no cavitation
legacy_cases_recovered.corrective_note: No open primary SOSUS telemetry supporting these numerical claims was located in this audit. Do not use as evidence until a traceable record is produced.
The 389 figure corresponds to Enigma coastal/water-adjacent reporting summaries from 2025, not 389 sonar-confirmed submerged objects. No sonar denominator or raw acoustic set is established.
The 306 figure was a regional reporting count, not a set of confirmed underwater sonar tracks. Military-base proximity is not an acoustic identification.

legacy_cases_recovered.use_in_cousteau: not acoustic evidence unless a traceable sonar record is recovered
military sensor-opportunity control, not underwater acoustic evidence

new_high_value_acoustic_controls.fact: WWII sonar operators observed an apparently moving false seafloor; later work identified the deep scattering layer of marine organisms as the reflector.
new_high_value_acoustic_controls.lesson: A strong coherent military sonar anomaly can be real data and still have a natural source.

new_high_value_acoustic_controls.fact: A repetitive mechanical-sounding underwater signal first named by submarine personnel in the 1960s remained unexplained for decades and was linked by multi-sensor acoustic tags to Antarctic minke whales in 2014.
new_high_value_acoustic_controls.lesson: Repeatability and apparent responsiveness do not by themselves establish technology.

new_high_value_acoustic_controls.fact: Later Soviet/Russian submarine recollections describe recurring quacking acoustic contacts and reported changes during active acoustic transmissions. A separate naval recollection interprets at least some encounters as active sonobuoys used with broader ASW systems.
new_high_value_acoustic_controls.lesson: This is the closest historical analogue to the proposed pyramid-resonator hypothesis, but it is not raw-data evidence and must remain ambiguous.

new_high_value_acoustic_controls.fact: Official U.S. Navy histories and professional literature document repeated false submarine contacts during antisubmarine operations and high false-contact rates for some active sonar contexts.
new_high_value_acoustic_controls.lesson: Military operations strongly increase both sensor opportunity and the number of false positives.

current_public_testimony_bridge.summary: Retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet testified that former submarine personnel described an anomalous 1980s sonar track that approached with torpedo-like closing rate, slowed to follow the submarine, then rapidly departed. He explicitly stated he had no personal submersible-object experience and was relaying witness accounts.
current_public_testimony_bridge.hotspot_statement: When asked about current North American hotspots, Gallaudet said he did not have sufficiently credible data.

janus_echo_cousteau_hypothesis.statement: A stationary submerged or buried structure could appear preferentially during military operations because active sonar provides the illuminating acoustic energy; the structure would scatter or ring rather than needing to emit spontaneously.
predictions_if_true: anomaly localizes repeatedly to the same geodetic seafloor point across different platforms and dates
signal strength or ringing increases during active insonification relative to matched passive periods
two-way travel time is consistent with a fixed reflector rather than a moving vehicle
after CTD sound-speed correction, modal ratios and phase structure remain stable
multi-aspect returns show repeatable orientation dependence
the same location recurs in independent sonar systems or passes
predictions_against: contact moves with sonobuoy geometry, ship, aircraft, or biological layer
frequency pattern follows transmitter waveform rather than a target transfer function
only one wartime/exercise encounter exists with no geographic repeat
known biology, reverberation, internal-wave or equipment artifact explains the return

military_data_inference_boundary.allowed: Military and ASW archives are high-value search targets because they contain dense active/passive acoustic observations collected under operational conditions.
military_data_inference_boundary.forbidden: Do not infer that militaries already possess pyramid locations merely because unresolved or classified sonar contacts exist.
military_data_inference_boundary.reason: Operational tempo is itself a major observation-opportunity and false-contact confound.
